items.title: Junior Mance Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995…
items.q: I did a record date once, why they asked me to do it to be honest I don’t know, with Buddy Guy and Junior Wells.

ctx.x: Not that many of them are still here, that’s too bad.

That’s true too. B.B. King, I’m glad he’s still around. B.B. King has opened a blues place, a blues club in Los Angeles that’s doing fantastic. And he has all the guys, some of the forgotten guys, he’ll give them a booking there. And in Chicago, Buddy Guy has a club there also now you know. And most of them, they call it Chicago blues, but they’re mostly youngsters who, when I listen to them, most of them are imitating. Some are influenced. You know there is a difference between being influenced and imitating.…
I mean did you feel like you had too much, I don’t know how to put this, too much knowledge from your bebop playing?
